### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Description

I am having issues with live grep on very large code bases.
The issue I believe is that rg is spawned for each key press (I may be wrong)
 if the result are in the hundreds of thousands. the plugin takes a lot of time to load the results into memory and the UI becomes non-responsive for few seconds.
This cycle repeats until the query string becomes longs enough and the result list get's shorter.

Unfortunately, I don't think rg have a switch to limit the total number of results.
What about implementing a throttle mechanism and a limit on the maximum number of results.

1 - throttle rg spawning while typing (for example: max 1 spawn per second)
2 - if rg takes longer than the throttle delay or if the result exceeds certain number of lines, then stop the process and show only the results so far and if the query changed meanwhile then start another rg.

comment_data.body: I can attempt a PR if this is something that makes sense to you.

Thanks for the issue!

I can see that happening, but I'd like to ask for the reproduction. If the delay is couple of seconds for 100K+ matches, I'd consider this okay-ish.

Optimizing speed for 100K+ matches is not really a goal for 'mini.pick', as at that range it is responsiveness that matters: user should be able to type the query and each key will get registered and processed (eventually).

Although `rg` indeed spawns after every query change, the previous process should be terminated immediately. If I know that there are a lot of files to search through, I tend to type initial keys fast so that to reach the state when there are manageable number of matches.

> Unfortunately, I don't think rg have a switch to limit the total number of results.

Total - no. But there is `--max-count` which might be occasionally useful.

I reproduced using the following steps

- git clone https://github.com/torvalds/linux.git
- NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax nvim
- :Pick grep_live
- press down and don't release a keyboard key (to generate a sequence of about 10 or more)
- Neovim becomes unresponsive for about 1 to 3 seconds 

This is a Mac M1, so mileage may vary depending on the hardware.
It was a little worse on my work computer.

> I reproduced using the following steps

Yep, so we are on the same page here. This is indeed a behavior that was/is considered "normal" here. Not "good", but somewhat expected.

The idea of introducing a delay (in 'mini.nvim' I usually prefer debounce type) might indeed be handy here. Some picker plugins have "minimum query length" for picker like this.

I'll think about the best way to approach this. Maybe the reason this happens is indeed with a misuse of `vim.uv.spawn`. After Neovim<0.10 compatibility is dropped, maybe moving to `vim.system` will improve things.

Hi @echasnovski , I think I may have found the root cause of the issue.
My findings is that the stale stdout buffers from the already killed processes were kept in memory and triggering 
stdout:read_start() in set_picker_items_from_cli()
which was hogging the libuv event loop

A simple way I got the issue to disappear is by adding an 'interrupt' flag as such

```
MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts, flags)
        .........
	local data_feed = {}
	stdout:read_start(function(err, data)
		assert(not err, err)
		if data ~= nil and not flags.interrupt then return table.insert(data_feed, data) end
		stdout:close()
		if not flags.interrupt then
			local items = vim.split(table.concat(data_feed), '\r?\n')
			data_feed = nil
			vim.schedule(function() MiniPick.set_picker_items(opts.postprocess(items), opts.set_items_opts) end)
		end
	end)
	return process, pid
end

```
and triggering it as such

```
	local flags = {}
	local match = function(_, _, query)
		flags.interrupt = true
		flags  = {}
		pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
		if H.querytick == set_items_opts.querytick then return end
		if #query == 0 then return MiniPick.set_picker_items({}, set_items_opts) end

		set_items_opts.querytick = H.querytick
		local command = H.grep_get_command(tool, table.concat(query), globs)
		local picker_opts = { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts };
		process = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, picker_opts, flags)
	end
```


The only issue I see now is when the the number of results is really large (may be around a million or more), which is likely with 1 or 2 char query, I that case, the process is stuck (for a long time with 100% CPU), again probably because the all the stdout buffer events are hugging the event loop.
So a hard limit on the results and stdout reading is really important I believe.

Please let me know if this makes sense to you. 
If so, you may want to do the fix in a way preferred by you based on this idea. 
Or suggest a method and I may be able to create a PR.

Cheers!

Edit: typos and formatting

> Hi [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski) , I think I may have found the root cause of the issue.
> My findings is that the stale stdout buffers from the already killed processes were kept in memory and triggering
> stdout:read_start() in set_picker_items_from_cli()
> which was hogging the libuv event loop

That's an interesting find and seems to be the case. I did manage to incorporate these changes and there is indeed big difference. Nice find! Handling CLI jobs/stdout/stderr is never my strong suite.

This indeed seems to fix the issue. I'm just relatively reluctant to add something to the public interface to handle this. Ideally this should be solveable with already present information. I am a bit surprised that using `process:is_closing()` or `process:is_active()` here instead of an explicit `flags.interrupt`.

I'll take a closer look some time later.

---

There is something off here. The `flags = {}` should probably go after `vim.loop.process_kill`, right?

> ```lua
> ...
> flags.interrupt = true
> flags  = {}
> pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
> ...
> ```

I used the following patch to see that this might fix the problem:

<details><summary>'mini.pick' patch</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/pick.lua b/lua/mini/pick.lua
index 5a5649d9..edd96767 100644
--- a/lua/mini/pick.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/pick.lua
@@ -1388,15 +1388,18 @@ MiniPick.builtin.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)
 
   local cwd = H.full_path(opts.source.cwd or vim.fn.getcwd())
   local set_items_opts, spawn_opts = { do_match = false, querytick = H.querytick }, { cwd = cwd }
-  local process
+  local process, flags = nil, {}
   local match = function(_, _, query)
+    flags.interrupt = true
     pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
+    flags = {}
     if H.querytick == set_items_opts.querytick then return end
     if #query == 0 then return MiniPick.set_picker_items({}, set_items_opts) end
 
     set_items_opts.querytick = H.querytick
     local command = H.grep_get_command(tool, table.concat(query), globs)
-    process = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts })
+    local picker_opts = { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts }
+    process = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, picker_opts, flags)
   end
 
   local add_glob = function()
@@ -1727,7 +1730,7 @@ end
 ---   - <set_items_opts> `(table)` - table forwarded to |MiniPick.set_picker_items()|.
 ---
 ---@seealso |MiniPick.get_picker_items()| and |MiniPick.get_picker_stritems()|
-MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
+MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts, flags)
   local is_valid_command = H.is_array_of(command, 'string') and #command >= 1
   if not is_valid_command then H.error('`command` should be an array of strings.') end
   local default_opts = { postprocess = H.cli_postprocess, set_items_opts = {}, spawn_opts = {} }
@@ -1748,6 +1751,10 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
 
   local data_feed = {}
   stdout:read_start(function(err, data)
+    if flags.interrupt then
+      data_feed = nil
+      return stdout:close()
+    end
     assert(not err, err)
     if data ~= nil then return table.insert(data_feed, data) end
 
```

</details>

> I used the following patch to see that this might fix the problem:

Glad that my finding is helpful.
Regarding the location of the `flags = {}`, that should not matter because every call to `set_picker_items_from_cli` will have it's own instance of the `flags` table, `interrupt = true` ill interrupt reading the std out of the previous process (not directly related to process_kill()), 
and setting flags to a new empty table is intended for the next process to be spawned by `set_picker_items_from_cli `

> Regarding the location of the `flags = {}`, that should not matter because every call to `set_picker_items_from_cli` will have it's own instance of the `flags` table, `interrupt = true` ill interrupt reading the std out of the previous process (not directly related to process_kill()),

Yeah, I realized that part (that `flags` is meant to be adjusted in-place in order to affect the process) later. This approach doesn't feel right to put into exported and documented behavior.

I would still like to see if manipulating strictly within `set_picker_items_from_cli` is possible. In principle, all that is needed is to detect early on when `process` is terminated with `process_kill` and act as if `flags.interrupt = true` branch.

Here is another 'cleaner' way without having to change the parameters,
this way you don't have to change the existing public documentation 


```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/pick.lua b/lua/mini/pick.lua
index 5a5649d9..77fe0dd0 100644
--- a/lua/mini/pick.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/pick.lua
@@ -1388,15 +1388,16 @@ MiniPick.builtin.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)

   local cwd = H.full_path(opts.source.cwd or vim.fn.getcwd())
   local set_items_opts, spawn_opts = { do_match = false, querytick = H.querytick }, { cwd = cwd }
-  local process
+  local process, interrupt
   local match = function(_, _, query)
+	if interrupt then interrupt() end
     pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
     if H.querytick == set_items_opts.querytick then return end
     if #query == 0 then return MiniPick.set_picker_items({}, set_items_opts) end

     set_items_opts.querytick = H.querytick
     local command = H.grep_get_command(tool, table.concat(query), globs)
-    process = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts })
+    process, _, interrupt = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts })
   end

   local add_glob = function()
@@ -1746,9 +1747,14 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
   local kill_process = function() pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process) end
   vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStop', once = true, callback = kill_process })

-  local data_feed = {}
+  local data_feed, interrupt_flag = {}, false
   stdout:read_start(function(err, data)
     assert(not err, err)
+    if interrupt_flag then
+      data_feed = nil
+      stdout:close()
+	  return
+	end
     if data ~= nil then return table.insert(data_feed, data) end

     local items = vim.split(table.concat(data_feed), '\r?\n')
@@ -1757,7 +1763,8 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
     vim.schedule(function() MiniPick.set_picker_items(opts.postprocess(items), opts.set_items_opts) end)
   end)

-  return process, pid
+  local interrupt = function() interrupt_flag = true end
+  return process, pid, interrupt
 end

 --- Set match indexes for active picker
```

It seems that `vim.loop.process_kill` does not mutable the process table in any way.
So it may not be possible to detect that the process received vim.loop.process_kill() directly using the available information inside `set_picker_items_from_cli`
But I may be wrong here.

If you do not find any other solution, and want to adopt the solution above with the interrupt() function returned,

you can make the interrupt() function set the interrupt_flag = true and also call process_kill() 

this way it can be documented as "call interrupt() to  interrupt the CLI output processing" (In case you add documentation about the return values, as right now I don't see any)

basically this:

```lua
  local interrupt = function() 
	  interrupt_flag = true 
      pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
  end
  return process, pid, interrupt

```

> Here is another 'cleaner' way without having to change the parameters,
> this way you don't have to change the existing public documentation

Yeah, something like that was what I thought about when posting the comment.

After thinking about it, I think the variant of this might be the way to go, but with a twist. In a (hopefully not so distant) future the whole 'mini.nvim' will move to use `vim.system` instead of `vim.loop.spaw`. In particular, when the compatibility with Neovim=0.9 is dropped. The `vim.system` returns an object with information about a system call. So the output of `set_picker_items_from_cli()` is reasonable to model after that for the time being.

Unfortunately, it doesn't look like there is an easy way to replicate this `interrupt` approach in `vim.system`. There is only `sys:kill()` which doesn't force stop

There is also no need for a flags, since it is possible to `stdout:read_stop()`

 I'll take it from here, thanks!

Okay, after experimenting for a bit, I think something like this might work:

<details><summary>More responsive `MiniPick.builtin.grep_live`</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/pick.lua b/lua/mini/pick.lua
index 32e630ca..af95990d 100644
--- a/lua/mini/pick.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/pick.lua
@@ -1391,5 +1391,5 @@ MiniPick.builtin.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)
   local set_items_opts, spawn_opts = { do_match = false, querytick = H.querytick }, { cwd = cwd }
-  local process
+  local sys = { cancel = function() end }
   local match = function(_, _, query)
-    pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process)
+    sys.cancel()
     if H.querytick == set_items_opts.querytick then return end
@@ -1399,3 +1399,3 @@ MiniPick.builtin.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)
     local command = H.grep_get_command(tool, table.concat(query), globs)
-    process = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts })
+    sys = MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli(command, { set_items_opts = set_items_opts, spawn_opts = spawn_opts })
   end
@@ -1738,14 +1738,22 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
   local executable, args = command[1], vim.list_slice(command, 2, #command)
-  local process, pid, stdout = nil, nil, vim.loop.new_pipe()
+  local stdout, data_feed = vim.loop.new_pipe(), {}
   local spawn_opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', opts.spawn_opts, { args = args, stdio = { nil, stdout, nil } })
   if type(spawn_opts.cwd) == 'string' then spawn_opts.cwd = H.full_path(spawn_opts.cwd) end
+
+  local process, pid
   process, pid = vim.loop.spawn(executable, spawn_opts, function()
-    if process:is_active() then process:close() end
+    -- NOTE: Do not move this into `cancel` and use `on_exit=cancel` here.
+    -- It leaves hanging processes.
+    if not process:is_closing() then process:close() end
   end)
+  local cancel = function()
+    if process:is_active() then process:kill() end
+    stdout:read_stop()
+    data_feed = nil
+    if not stdout:is_closing() then stdout:close() end
+  end
 
-  -- Make sure to stop the process if picker is stopped
-  local kill_process = function() pcall(vim.loop.process_kill, process) end
-  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStop', once = true, callback = kill_process })
+  -- Make sure to cancel the process if picker is stopped
+  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStop', once = true, callback = cancel })
 
-  local data_feed = {}
   stdout:read_start(function(err, data)
@@ -1755,4 +1763,3 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
     local items = vim.split(table.concat(data_feed), '\r?\n')
-    data_feed = nil
-    stdout:close()
+    cancel()
     vim.schedule(function() MiniPick.set_picker_items(opts.postprocess(items), opts.set_items_opts) end)
@@ -1760,3 +1767,3 @@ MiniPick.set_picker_items_from_cli = function(command, opts)
 
-  return process, pid
+  return { pid = pid, cancel = cancel }
 end
```

</details>

There is still a hang after typing two letter query in 'torwarlds/linux' and waiting for awhile. But I think it comes from how 'mini.pick' operates. In particular, [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/4f53281c51ad9384ef790178b9643740fa763979/lua/mini/pick.lua#L2334-L2339) (although it should be throttled).

I'll be daily driving this change for some time to see if there are any issues. Would you mind also confirming that this patch fixes things on your side?

Yes I confirm this patch fixes the main issue on my side too. 

For the second issue where typing a characters or two hangs the process, I believe this is because the large amount of stdout text sent to neovim overwhelms the internal event loop.
for example, 
when typing 'zz' which is uncommon sequence, the result output is very quick (few thousands results)
when typing 'ma' which is fairly common in code, neovim is stuck about 20 seconds or more (5 million results).
when typing 'in' which is very common in code, neovim is stuck in 100% CPU for minutes in my case (about 11 million results).

So in my opinion, a hard limit on on the amount of data parsed or the number of results is required 

Proof of concept code that fixes the issue

```lua
	local bytes = 0
	stdout:read_start(function(err, data)
		assert(not err, err)
		bytes = bytes + #data
		if data ~= nil and bytes < 10000000 then
			return table.insert(data_feed, data)
		end
		local items = vim.split(table.concat(data_feed), '\r?\n')
		cancel()
		vim.schedule(function() MiniPick.set_picker_items(opts.postprocess(items), opts.set_items_opts) end)
	end)

```

 
-- Edited to fix typos

> So in my opinion, a hard limit on on the amount of data parsed or the number of results is required

I don't think it is a good idea to add that. As there is no good rule of thumb to set this universally int the config. At least because this might differ from project to project. There is also a problem that output order of `rg` is not deterministic, so it will be somewhat confusing.

What looks like happening is that the `stdout` gets read in full, but `vim.split(table.concat(data_feed), '\r?\n')` is blocking the picker from processing any next key press. And for many matches this will be computing for a relatively long time.

Could you please check the [`backlog` branch](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/tree/backlog), which has two commits that should make this issue more or less addressed. Optimizing for extreme number of items is not really the goal for 'mini.pick' in the first place. The rough goal is to "feel almost instant below 100K, bearable at 1M, as non-blocking as possible above it".

This should now be resolved on latest `main`. The adjustment was indeed two part:
- Properly stop the CLI process before the next match.
- Make converting from stdout chunks into items more responsive with coroutine magic. 

The first one makes it possible to respond to user key press *before* stdout is finished, while second one -*after*. I did quick experiments and overall I think the second has bigger impact, but both are needed for smoother experience.

Thank you again for finding one of the culprits and discussing it here! I had in mind to indeed introduce debouncing, but this feels much better.

---

Also note for the future self. It seems that with `vim.system()`, calling its `:kill()` method is enough to fully stop the process. Although after reading its code I still couldn't quite figure out why it worked there but not in the previous version of 'mini.pick'. There was only a single `read_stop()` which was done *after* all stdout chunks are read.
Having the non-blocking `stdout` is still needed for responsiveness, though.

Thank you for the your work, It's much better now. 
I tested on my MacBook and I found no issues.

I noticed an issue on my work machine (linux with neovim install via conda (non standard build))
The issue happens when typing a 2 characters query with more than 1 million of candidates.
while it's loading (after few seconds) and before the result is shown, I continue typing other queries.
I noticed the live grep window became sluggish after this and CPU usage remained high (around 25% or more) without improvement after minutes.

I could not reproduce this on my MacOS. so it could be due to old OS or weird or old neovim build.
If you cannot reproduce this yourself, we can assume that everything is working fine now.

Cheers!

> I noticed the live grep window became sluggish after this and CPU usage remained high (around 25% or more) without improvement after minutes.
> 
> I could not reproduce this on my MacOS. so it could be due to old OS or weird or old neovim build. If you cannot reproduce this yourself, we can assume that everything is working fine now.

I did encounter sluggishness during testing after:
1. Typing something like `in` inside 'torvalds/linux'.
2. Waiting a bit to the point when the `nvim` process at 99% CPU. This is usually at the stage when items are being prepared for the picker ([here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/c163117900c17d4abf30bc09452a261c8536060c/lua/mini/pick.lua#L2345)). This takes visible amount of time for large number of inputs and is an intended compromise between "pre-compute once now" vs "compute several time on the fly later". This probably won't change, but I might have a few ideas now.
3. Keep typing the query. It feels not instant. My guess is that there is too much RAM usage going on and it needs affect how Neovim works.
